Korosten Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Zhytomyrska oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Korosten — known as Iskorost until the early 20th century — had a Jewish leaseholder as early as 1618, though a larger community only emerged in the 19th century. In 1926, the town hosted a conference of 90 Ukrainian rabbis attended by 1,500 guests, even as an underground cheder continued operating; in 1925, Korosten's Jews founded seven agricultural colonies in the Kherson District. This record contains a contradiction worth flagging: it is officially categorized as a cemetery 'that has not been built over,' yet its own site notes describe the location as now occupied by a kindergarten, a school's sports ground, and a block of flats — the cemetery was in fact demolished in 1960, not long after a school and sports ground were built there, with some tombstones transferred to the Jewish sector of the municipal cemetery. About 200 local Jews fought with partisans during WWII, and a synagogue, mikveh, and yeshiva were newly opened in Korosten in 1995, even as most of the community was emigrating to Israel or the US.
